headline: Apple orders 10M foldable iPhone Ultra models, could sell for around $2500, report says
summary: A new report suggests Apple is planning a significant entry into the foldable market, with a high-end 'Ultra' model potentially priced at $2500.
details: Apple plans to manufacture and sell around 10 million foldable iPhone Ultra models, according to a new report. This significant order indicates Apple's serious intent to enter the foldable smartphone market, with a rumored price of around $2500.
The 'iPhone Fold' is also expected to boost foldable phone panel shipments, per industry reports. This suggests a broader impact on the supply chain and the overall foldable device segment.
caption:
Apple is reportedly preparing to launch a foldable iPhone Ultra, with an initial order of 10 million units.

Apple plans to manufacture and sell around 10 million foldable iPhone Ultra models, according to a new report. This significant order indicates Apple's serious intent to enter the foldable smartphone market, with a rumored price of around $2500.

The 'iPhone Fold' is also expected to boost foldable phone panel shipments, per industry reports. This suggests a broader impact on the supply chain and the overall foldable device segment.

headline_marked: [[T-Mobile sues Broadcom]] over VMware support, moving tens of thousands of VMs
headline: T-Mobile sues Broadcom over VMware support, moving tens of thousands of VMs
summary: T-Mobile is taking legal action against Broadcom for allegedly refusing to honor extended support for its VMware perpetual licenses, impacting tens of thousands of virtual machines.
details: T-Mobile has filed a lawsuit against Broadcom in New York, seeking continued support for its VMware perpetual licenses. The telecom giant operates tens of thousands of virtual machines on VMware software, spanning over 300,000 CPU cores.

The dispute arose after Broadcom acquired VMware, subsequently ending sales of perpetual licenses in favor of subscription models and more expensive bundles. T-Mobile claims Broadcom refused to extend support for a third year, despite a contractual option.
A judge granted T-Mobile an injunction, ensuring support services from October 2025 through August 2026 for $5.28 million. T-Mobile also had to post a $500,000 undertaking as part of the ruling.

T-Mobile previously offered $20 million for two years of updates, citing security risks and business interruption. Broadcom, however, claims it incurred $24 million in costs to provide support for six VMware products and dedicated account managers.

T-Mobile disputes Broadcom's cost claims, stating it uses only three of the six named products and opened only two service cases this year. Broadcom argues T-Mobile is an outlier, as thousands of other customers have successfully migrated to subscriptions.
